messages:
leah: Noticed a sharp spike in apiserver 5xxs in eu-central starting ~02:05 UTC. Correlated with etcd WAL fsync 99p jumping to ~2.8s. GPU onboarding tasks time out and fall back to hosted pools.

infra-bot: [ALERT] etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds p99=2.8s (eu-central)

tom: Oof. Any recent kernel or disk changes on those controlplane nodes?

arjun: We did a maintenance kernel upgrade last night on a subset of controlplane VMs (k8s infra update). Seeing increased write latency on their nvme devices in monitoring for the same hosts.

leah: Logs from apiserver/controller-manager around 02:06: see repeated timeouts acquiring leases and apiserver returning 503s: 

```
E0322 02:06:12.987 apiserver.go:210] unable to handle request: net/http: request canceled while waiting for response
I0322 02:06:13.003 leaderelection.go:243] failed to renew lease: timed out waiting for the condition
E0322 02:06:13.004 controller_manager.go:118] leader election lost: etcd request timed out
```

leah: GPU provisioner pods move to Pending because controller-manager isn't processing node allocations. Scheduler shows backlog of nodeBindings.

tom: Fast mitigation options we can do right now: 1) cordon and migrate controlplane pods off hosts with nvme tail latency 2) temporarily promote a standby etcd node onto a faster disk 3) increase leaderElection leaseDuration to 60s in staging then prod.

arjun: I can remount WAL to a separate higher-iops disk for etcd on the 3 affected nodes, flip them one at a time, and watch p99. That should drop fsync down below 200ms.

leah: Cost impact: we saw ~210k tokens routed to hosted fallback during the 40m window while provisioning was impaired. Finance estimate ~ $620 incremental. Need to include that in postmortem.

tom: Also: add a proactive alert that watches etcd WAL fsync > 1s for > 2m and fires a SEV1 candidate for controlplane owners. Right now infra-bot only alerts at 3s.

leah: Small safety net: for GPU provisioning controllers we can add a short client-side retry with exponential backoff so short leader blips don't immediately cause full fallback to hosted pools. We'll need to be careful about amplifying load on the API though.

arjun: I'm going to start the WAL move now. Plan: 1) cordon controlplane node A, 2) stop etcd and kubelet, 3) move /var/lib/etcd/wal to nvme-fast1, 4) restart etcd, 5) monitor etcd_disk_wal_fsync_duration_seconds p99. Repeat nodes B,C. Expected time ~ 12m/node.

infra-bot: action-created: infra-action-20260322-78 (owner: arjun, ETA: 36m)

tom: After that, we should run a staged leaderElection parameter change in staging: leaseDuration=60s, renewDeadline=40s, retryPeriod=10s. If stable, roll to eu-central. Document rollback plan.

leah: I'll open a short runbook section: "etcd WAL: kernel-related tail latency causing controlplane lease flaps" with commands to detect orphaned leases, migrate WAL, and calculate cost delta.

arjun: WAL move in progress on node A. Early numbers look promising: p99 dropped from 2.8s -> 180ms after switch.

leah: Nice. Once all three nodes are on fast disk and leaderElection changes staged, follow-ups: - tom: create the new etcd fsync alert and update paging rules - arjun: finish WAL moves + verify restore test - leah: draft postmortem including cost spreadsheet

infra-bot: incident-created: INC-20260322-79 (severity: medium). Runbook draft: https://intranet.redwood/runbooks/etcd-wal-tail-latency

leah: I'll post a short update when eu-central is fully stabilized. Thanks for the quick pivot, team :rocket:
